- A prominent milblogger claimed on 2026-07-06 that he was removed following the Kupiansk failures. [c900022]

Bottom line: He was reportedly dismissed, but there is no official confirmation at this time. [c900021][c900022]

- OpenSanctions lists Elena Shubina as a relative or close associate (role.rca) of the designated businessman Pyotr Shubin; she is not herself designated [c900041].  
- The linkage matters because OFAC designated Pyotr Shubin in 2024 for sanctions evasion on behalf of a designated bank [c900042].  
- The association with Shubin is reported by OpenSanctions (assessed), while Shubin’s OFAC designation is confirmed [c900041][c900042].

The evidence is insufficient to determine whether the businessman Oleg Danilov is on a sanctions list. The available data reflects only a name-level match, with identity unresolved; without unique identifiers (e.g., birthdate or other corroborating details), we cannot confirm this is the same individual.

Aurora Logistics LLC was reportedly removed from the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list on 2026-03-18 after a successful delisting petition [c900061]. Based on that delisting, it is not currently sanctioned by OFAC as of that date [c900061].

- Ukrainian media reported the arrest of a Serhiy Bondar identified as a territorial defense battalion commander near Odesa on 2026-07-01, but this is an unverified, low-reliability claim [c900071].
- A separate, higher-reliability, confirmed report shows Serhiy Bondar, the deputy head of the Odesa port authority, attending an infrastructure coordination meeting in Kyiv on 2026-07-03 [c900072].
- Given the confirmed public appearance of the port official two days later and the low-reliability nature of the arrest report, there is no confirmed evidence that the Odesa port authority official was arrested; the arrest report may pertain to a different individual with the same name [c900071] [c900072].
